results.title: Valuations extending a prime-adic valuation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $K$, let $L$ be a field extension of $K$, and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$. A valuation $w$ on $L$ with values in the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Z}$ with a zero adjoined extends the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of $K$ when its restriction to $K$ is equivalent to the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic valuation of $K$.

results.title: Height-one primes above a prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains with $B$ an $A$-algebra, and let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$. The primes above $\mathfrak{p}$ form the set of height-one primes $\mathfrak{q}$ of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$, that is, whose preimage in $A$ is $\mathfrak{p}$.

results.title: Membership in a prime is detected by a prime lying over it
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be Dedekind domains with $B$ an $A$-algebra, let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime of $A$, and let $\mathfrak{q}$ be a height-one prime of $B$ lying over $\mathfrak{p}$. Then for every $a \in A$, $a \in \mathfrak{p}$ if and only if the image of $a$ in $B$ lies in $\mathfrak{q}$.

results.title: A valuation centered at a height-one prime is equivalent to its adic valuation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $B$ be a Dedekind domain with fraction field $L$, let $\mathfrak{q}$ be a height-one prime of $B$, and let $w$ be a valuation on $L$ with values in the multiplicative group $\mathbb{Z}$ with a zero adjoined. Suppose that $w(b) \le 1$ for every $b \in B$, and that for every $b \in B$ we have $b \in \mathfrak{q}$ if and only if $w(b) < 1$. Then the $\mathfrak{q}$-adic valuation of $L$ is equivalent to $w$.

results.title: Coordinate restriction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras indexed by a type $\iota$. For a finite subset $S \subseteq \iota$, the coordinate restriction is the $K$-algebra homomorphism $\prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to \prod_{i \in S} F_i$ sending $(x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ to $(x_i)_{i \in S}$.

results.title: A surjective image of a finite product of fields is isomorphic to a subproduct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, $\iota$ a finite type, $(F_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of fields that are $K$-algebras, and $B$ a commutative $K$-algebra. If $\varphi : \prod_{i \in \iota} F_i \to B$ is a surjective $K$-algebra homomorphism, then there is a finite subset $S \subseteq \iota$ such that $B$ is isomorphic as a $K$-algebra to $\prod_{i \in S} F_i$.

results.title: Uniqueness of a finite product of fields up to permutation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field, and let $(F_i)_{i \in I}$ and $(G_j)_{j \in J}$ be families of fields that are $K$-algebras, indexed by finite types $I$ and $J$. If $e : \prod_{i \in I} F_i \to \prod_{j \in J} G_j$ is an isomorphism of $K$-algebras, then there is a bijection $\sigma : I \to J$ such that $F_i$ is isomorphic to $G_{\sigma(i)}$ as a $K$-algebra for every $i \in I$.

results.title: Product decompositions and idempotents
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A commutative ring $Q$ is isomorphic to a product $R \times S$ of two nontrivial rings $R$ and $S$ if and only if $Q$ contains an idempotent $e$ with $e \neq 0$ and $e \neq 1$.

results.title: Sparse admissible sets without prime translates (Erdős Problem 429)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $f(N) \to \infty$ as $N \to \infty$, there is an infinite set $A$ of natural numbers such that $|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| \le f(N)$ for every natural number $N$, for every prime $p$ some residue class modulo $p$ contains no element of $A$, and for every integer $n$ some $a \in A$ makes $n + a$ not a positive prime.

results.title: Sparse subsets of powers with no prime translate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a$ be a natural number that is a primitive root modulo infinitely many primes, and let $S = \{a^k : k \ge 1\}$. For every non-decreasing unbounded function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ there is an infinite set $A \subseteq S$ such that $|A \cap \{1, \dots, N\}| \le f(N)$ for every natural number $N$, and such that no translate $A + n$ with $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ consists entirely of (positive) primes.

results.title: Overpartitions of $5n$ modulo $5$, explicit form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, the number of pairs $(P, S)$, where $P$ is a finite multiset of positive integers with sum $5n$ and $S$ is a finite set of natural numbers each belonging to $P$, is congruent modulo $5$ to $(-1)^n$ times the number of ordered triples $(x, y, z)$ of integers with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = n$.

results.title: Overpartitions as pairs of a multiset and a set
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For every natural number $m$, the number of overpartitions of $m$ equals the number of pairs $(P, S)$ in which $P$ is a finite multiset of positive integers with sum $m$ and $S$ is a finite set of natural numbers each belonging to $P$.

results.title: The three-square count counts all integer solutions

results.title: Overpartitions of $5n$ modulo $5$

results.title: Liang's congruences modulo 512 for overpartitions

results.title: Straight-line planar embedding
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A map $p$ from the vertex set of a simple graph $G$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a crossing-free straight-line embedding of $G$ if $p$ is injective, the closed segments $[p(u), p(v)]$ and $[p(x), p(y)]$ of any two different edges $uv$ and $xy$ meet only in points $p(z)$ with $z$ an endpoint of both edges, and no vertex $w$ other than $u$ and $v$ has $p(w)$ on the segment $[p(u), p(v)]$ of an edge $uv$.

results.title: Universal point set for planar graphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ is universal for $n$-vertex planar graphs if every straight-line planar simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has a crossing-free straight-line embedding $p$ with $p(v) \in P$ for every vertex $v$.

results.title: Subquadratic universal point sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $f(n)/n^2 \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n$ some finite set of at most $f(n)$ points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a universal point set for $n$-vertex planar graphs.

results.title: Planar graphs have subquadratic universal point sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $f(n)/n^2 \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ such that for every $n$ some finite set $P$ of at most $f(n)$ points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a universal point set for $n$-vertex planar graphs: every straight-line planar simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has a crossing-free straight-line embedding with all its vertices in $P$.

results.title: Binary encoding, least significant bit first
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \neq 0$, the binary encoding of $n$ is the list whose first bit is true exactly when $n$ is odd, followed by the binary encoding of $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$.

results.title: Value of a little-endian bit list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The value of a list of bits $b_0, b_1, \dots, b_{m-1}$ is $\sum_{i < m} [b_i]\, 2^i$, where $[b_i]$ is $1$ if $b_i$ is true and $0$ otherwise. So the first bit is the least significant, and the empty list has value $0$.

Then the partial function sending $a$ to $\mathrm{out}(\mathrm{step}^k(\mathrm{init}(a)))$, where $k$ is the least natural number for which…

results.title: Eventually constant functions on ℕ are primitive recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\beta$ be a primitive recursively encodable type. If $g : \mathbb{N} \to \beta$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $g(c) = g(N)$ for all $c \ge N$, then $g$ is primitive recursive.

results.title: Eventually constant functions of a finite parameter are primitive recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite primitive recursively encodable type and $\beta$ a primitive recursively encodable type. If $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{N} \to \beta$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $g(a, c) = g(a, N)$ for all $a \in \alpha$ and all $c \ge N$, then $g$ is primitive recursive as a function of two arguments.

results.title: Joint primitive recursion over a finite first argument
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\sigma$ be primitive recursively encodable types with $\alpha$ finite, and let $g : \alpha \to \beta \to \sigma$. If $b \mapsto g(a, b)$ is primitive recursive for every $a \in \alpha$, then $g$ is primitive recursive as a function of two arguments.

results.title: Encoding of functions on a finite type
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite type $K$ and a primitive recursively encodable type $\beta$, the primitive recursive encoding of the functions $K \to \beta$ transported from that of the functions $\mathrm{Fin}\, n \to \beta$, where $n$ is the cardinality of $K$, along a chosen bijection between $K$ and $\mathrm{Fin}\, n$.

results.title: Symbols a statement may push
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite multi-stack machine, a stack $k$ and a statement $q$ over the machine's stack alphabets, labels and internal states, the set of symbols of stack $k$ consisting of every value, at every internal state, of the symbol function of every push instruction onto stack $k$ that occurs in $q$, in either branch of each conditional.

results.title: Relevant symbols of a stack
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a stack index $k$, the relevant symbols of stack $k$ are the symbols $f(v)$ of $\Gamma_k$, for every internal state $v$, over all statements that push $f$ onto stack $k$ and occur in the program of some label, together with, when $k$ is the input stack $k_0$, every symbol of $\Gamma_{k_0}$.

results.title: Enumeration of the relevant symbols of a stack
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite multi-stack machine and a stack index $k$, a list without repetitions whose entries are exactly the relevant symbols of stack $k$, in an order fixed by choice.

results.title: Code of a stack symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite multi-stack machine, a stack index $k$ and a symbol $x$ of stack $k$, the code of $x$ is the position of $x$ (counting from $0$) in the chosen enumeration of the relevant symbols of stack $k$, or the length of that enumeration if $x$ is not a relevant symbol.

results.title: Decoding a stack symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite multi-stack machine, a stack index $k$ and a natural number $c$, the decoding of $c$ is the entry at position $c$ (counting from $0$) of the chosen enumeration of the relevant symbols of stack $k$, and is undefined when $c$ is at least the length of that enumeration.

results.title: Stacks with only relevant symbols
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A family of stacks $S$, consisting of a list $S_k$ of symbols of $\Gamma_k$ for each stack index $k$, has only relevant symbols when for every stack index $k$, every symbol on $S_k$ is a relevant symbol of stack $k$.

results.title: Encoding of labels
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite multi-stack machine, the primitive recursive encoding of its finite type of labels transported from that of $\mathrm{Fin}\, n$, where $n$ is the number of labels, along a chosen bijection between the two.

results.title: Encoding of internal states
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite multi-stack machine, the primitive recursive encoding of its finite type of internal states transported from that of $\mathrm{Fin}\, n$, where $n$ is the number of internal states, along a chosen bijection between the two.

results.title: Coded configurations of a multi-stack machine
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a finite multi-stack machine with label set $\Lambda$, internal state set $\sigma$ and stack index set $K$, a coded configuration is a triple consisting of an optional label in $\Lambda$ (no label marks a halted configuration), an internal state in $\sigma$, and an assignment of a list of natural numbers to each $k \in K$.

results.title: Coded stacks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite multi-stack machine, the coded stacks of a family $S$ of stacks assign to each stack index $k$ the list obtained from the stack $S_k$ by replacing each symbol with its code.

results.title: Coding a configuration
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite multi-stack machine, the coded configuration of a configuration $c$ has the same optional label and internal state as $c$, and the coded stacks of the stacks of $c$.

results.title: Reading the top of a coded stack
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Description length of a code
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a code $c$ of a partial recursive function, the description length of $c$ is the number of binary digits of the encoding of $c$ as a natural number, that is, the least $k$ such that this encoding is less than $2^k$ (so it is $0$ when the encoding is $0$).

results.title: Minimal codes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A code $c$ of a partial recursive function is minimal when no code with a shorter description has the same domain: for every code $d$ whose description length is strictly less than that of $c$, the domain of $d$ (the set of inputs on which its evaluation is defined) differs from the domain of $c$. The set of minimal codes is denoted $\mathrm{MIN}$.

results.title: Codes with singleton domain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ there is a code $c$ of a partial recursive function whose evaluation is defined exactly at $n$, that is, the domain of the partial function computed by $c$ is $\{n\}$.

results.title: Every language of a code has a minimal code
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every code $c$ of a partial recursive function there is a minimal code $D$ whose domain equals the domain of $c$, where the domain of a code is the set of inputs on which its evaluation is defined.

results.title: Minimal codes are unbounded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $N$ there is a minimal code $D$ of a partial recursive function whose encoding as a natural number is greater than $N$.

results.title: Minimal codes are not recognizable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The set $\mathrm{MIN}$ of minimal codes of partial recursive functions is not recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine: there is no finite multi-stack machine that, for every code $c$, halts on the binary encoding of the natural-number encoding of $c$ exactly when $c$ is minimal.

results.title: Round of prediction with expert advice
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A round with $n$ experts is a pair $(a, y)$, where $a$ assigns to each expert $i \in \{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ its binary advice (true or false) and the binary value $y$ is the true outcome.

results.title: Weight on an answer
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given weights $w_0, \dots, w_{n-1}$ in a field $K$, advice $a \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n$ and an answer $b \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$, the weight on $b$ is $\sum_{i : a_i = b} w_i$, the total weight of the experts advising $b$.

results.title: Weighted majority vote
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order. Given weights in $K$ on $n$ experts and a binary advice (true or false) from each expert, the weighted majority vote is true when the total weight of the experts advising false is at most the total weight of the experts advising true, and false otherwise. In particular ties go to true.

results.title: Weighted majority update
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a penalty factor $\beta$ and weights $w_0, \dots, w_{n-1}$ in a field $K$, and a round with advice $a \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n$ and outcome $y$, the updated weight of expert $i$ is $w_i$ if $a_i = y$ and $\beta w_i$ otherwise: after the outcome is revealed, every expert that was wrong has its weight multiplied by $\beta$.

results.title: Weights after a run
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a penalty factor $\beta$ in a field $K$, the weights after a sequence of rounds $r_1, \dots, r_k$ starting from weights $w$ in $K$ are obtained by applying the weighted majority update with penalty $\beta$ for $r_1$, then for $r_2$, and so on up to $r_k$; for the empty sequence they are $w$.

results.title: Mistakes of an expert
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list of rounds with $n$ experts and an expert $i$, the number of mistakes of $i$ is the number of rounds in the list in which the advice of expert $i$ differs from the true outcome.

results.title: Total weight
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total weight of weights $w_0, \dots, w_{n-1}$ in a field $K$ is $\sum_{i < n} w_i$.

results.title: Total weight after an update
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\beta$ be an element of a linearly ordered field $K$, let $w_0, \dots, w_{n-1} \in K$ be weights on $n$ experts, and let $r$ be a round with advice $a \in \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}^n$ and outcome $y$. If $w'$ are the weights after the update with penalty $\beta$ on $r$, then $\sum_{i < n} w'_i = \sum_{i < n} w_i - (1 - \beta) \sum_{i : a_i = \lnot y} w_i$: the experts that advised wrongly keep a…

results.title: A mistake costs weight
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field, let $\beta \in K$ with $\beta \le 1$, let $w$ be weights in $K$ on $n$ experts, and let $r$ be a round on which the weighted majority vote under $w$ differs from the true outcome. If $W$ is the total weight of $w$ and $W'$ is the total weight after updating $w$ on $r$ with penalty $\beta$, then $2 W' \le (1 + \beta) W$.

results.title: An update never increases the total weight
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field, let $\beta \in K$ with $\beta \le 1$, and let $w$ be nonnegative weights in $K$ on $n$ experts. For every round $r$, the total weight after updating $w$ on $r$ with penalty $\beta$ is at most the total weight of $w$.

results.title: Total weight bound in terms of mistakes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $0 \le \beta \le 1$ in a linearly ordered field $K$, let $w$ be nonnegative weights in $K$ on $n$ experts, and let $\rho$ be a sequence of rounds. Let $M$ be the number of mistakes the weighted majority algorithm with penalty $\beta$ makes on $\rho$ starting from $w$, and let $W$ and $W'$ be the total weights before and after $\rho$. Then $W' \cdot 2^M \le (1 + \beta)^M \cdot W$.

results.title: Final weight of an expert
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a penalty factor $\beta$ in a field $K$, initial weights $w_0, \dots, w_{n-1} \in K$ and a sequence of rounds, the weight of expert $i$ after these rounds is $w_i \beta^{m_i}$, where $m_i$ is the number of rounds in which the advice of expert $i$ differs from the outcome.

results.title: Littlestone–Warmuth mistake bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and let $\beta \in K$ with $0 \le \beta \le 1$. Run the weighted majority algorithm with penalty $\beta$ on a list of rounds with $n$ experts, starting from weight $1$ on every expert, and let $M$ be its number of mistakes. Then every expert $i$, with $m$ mistakes on these rounds, satisfies $\beta^m 2^M \le n (1 + \beta)^M$.

results.title: Mistake bound for the penalty $1/2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Run the weighted majority algorithm with rational weights and penalty $1/2$ on a list of rounds with $n$ experts, starting from weight $1$ on every expert, and let $M$ be its number of mistakes. Then every expert $i$, with $m$ mistakes on these rounds, satisfies $(4/3)^M \le n \cdot 2^m$.

results.title: Mistake bound for the penalty $1/2$ in integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Run the weighted majority algorithm with rational weights and penalty $1/2$ on a list of rounds with $n$ experts, starting from weight $1$ on every expert, and let $M$ be its number of mistakes. Then every expert $i$, with $m$ mistakes on these rounds, satisfies $4^M \le n \cdot 3^M \cdot 2^m$ in the natural numbers.

results.title: Weights over a concatenated run
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a penalty factor $\beta$ in a field $K$, initial weights $w$ in $K$ and sequences of rounds $\rho$ and $\rho'$, the weights after running $\rho$ followed by $\rho'$ from $w$ equal the weights after running $\rho'$ from the weights obtained by running $\rho$ from $w$.

results.title: Mistakes split over concatenated runs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order, let $\beta \in K$ be a penalty, let $w$ be weights in $K$ on $n$ experts, and let $R$ and $R'$ be lists of rounds. The number of mistakes of the weighted majority algorithm with penalty $\beta$ on $R$ followed by $R'$, starting from $w$, equals its number of mistakes on $R$ starting from $w$ plus its number of mistakes on $R'$ starting from the weights reached after $R$.
